name: Sunny Varkey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Son of Indian expat teachers, who migrated to Dubai in 1959, Sunny Varkey controls GEMS Education, one of the world's largest operators of K-12 schools.
The private education firm secured CVC Capital Partners as its key investor in 2019. CVC is selling a part of its stake.
Sons Dino and Jay run GEMS as group CEO and deputy CEO, respectively.

In June 2024 it got a $2 billion investment from a consortium led by New York-based Brookfield Asset Management. Other investors included Dubai financial services firm Gulf Islamic Investments, private equity outfit Marathon Asset Management and the State Oil Fund of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
forbes_facts: Varkey, who never went beyond high school himself, took over the management of his parents' Our Own English School in 1980 at age 23.
GEMS has instituted three awards to recognize outstanding teachers, including one named after Varkey's mother.

name: Joel Greenberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Greenberg is a cofounder of Susquehanna International Group, one of Wall Street's largest and most successful trading firms.
Greenberg met Jeff Yass, his billionaire cofounder, at SUNY Binghamton in the late 1970s.
A lawyer educated at Columbia University, Greenberg served as Susquehanna's chief operating officer after cofounding the firm in 1987.
Susquehanna has invested in hundreds of private companies globally, including TikTok parent ByteDance, its most valuable holding based on Forbes reporting.

name: Akio Nitori
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Akio Nitori founded discount home furnishings chain Nitori Holdings; its shares trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The company has expanded in urban markets like Tokyo and has more than 1,000 stores mostly in Japan.
Nitori, the firm's chairman, opened the first store in 1967. He stepped down as president in 2016.
The chain has stores outside Japan in China, Taiwan, South Korea, India and several Southeast Asian countries.
forbes_facts: To earn money for college tuition and expenses, he worked collecting unpaid bar tabs and hustling pool, among other jobs.
In 2020, the company acquired home-improvement chain Shimachu in a nearly $2 billion deal.

name: Li Hu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Li Hu is the chairman of Shenzhen Techwinsemi Technology, a supplier of memory and storage products.
Li cofounded the company in 2008 and took it public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2022.
Li's wife, Tian Hua, sits on the board.

name: Henry Swieca
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: A Wall Street veteran, Henry Swieca cofounded hedge fund firm Highbridge Capital Management in 1992 with childhood friend Glenn Dubin.
The duo sold part of the business to JP Morgan Chase in 2004 and the rest in 2009.
After the sale Swieca opened Talpion Fund, which manages his own fortune. The name Talpion comes from the Biblical word Talpiot, meaning a castle's turret.
Talpion's portfolio includes real estate and startup cash for new money management firms.
A son of Polish holocaust survivors, Swieca started off his career at Merrill Lynch, where he got the job by knocking on the doors of Manhattan banks.
forbes_facts: Swieca learned stock investing from his dentist uncle, and turned to the market to fund his and his brother's education after losing both of his parents at age 19.
Highbridge was named after an aqueduct that connected New York City's Washington Heights (where Swieca was raised) and the Bronx.

name: Dorothy Chao Jenkins
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Dorothy Chao Jenkins is estimated to own nearly 25% of Westlake Corporation, one of North America's largest producers of low-density polyethylene, used for food packaging and more.
Her father T.T. Chao moved the family from Taiwan to the U.S. and founded Westlake in 1986. Her brothers James and Albert are credited with helping launch the company.
James and Albert co-chair the company's board. They're each estimated to own nearly 25% of Westlake.
Dorothy is married to Charles H. Jenkins, Jr., the former chairman of his family's supermarket chain, Publix. She retired as a director of Westlake in 2023.
Four of her nieces and nephews sit on the company's board.

name: Brian Hill
sec_insider_companies: APPLIED MATERIALS INC /DE (AMAT) - SVP, CFO; PACCAR INC (PCAR) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Brian Hill is the founder of the Vancouver-based women's fashion retailer Aritzia, popular for its "everyday luxury" clothing.
The son of a Vancouver department store owner, Hill opened his Aritzia first store in 1984 at age 23. He took the company public in Toronto in 2016.
Today, Aritzia's around 130 "boutiques" across Canada and the U.S. generate nearly $2 billion in annual revenue.
Hill ran the company as CEO for 38 years before stepping down in 2022; he remains executive chair.
He owns around 16% of the company's stock.
forbes_facts: Hill's father owned the Hill's of Kerrisdale, a department store in Vancouver, while his grandfather ran a dry goods store in the city.
Hill worked as a garbageman for three months before opening the first Aritzia in a Vancouver mall.

name: Julio Bozano
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Julio Bozano made a fortune in banking. In 2000, he sold Banco Bozano, Simonsen to Spain's Banco Santander Central Hispano for a reported $550 million.
His investments include a coffee plantation, shopping centers and a stake in a jet engine maker.
Octogenarian Bozano controls Bozano Investimentos, a large and diversified Brazilian private equity firm.
He invested in low-cost Brazilian airline, Azul Linhas Aereas, which was founded by JetBlue founder David Neeleman and went public in April 2017.
A thoroughbred horse owner, Bozano owns more than 300 mares in farms around the world.
forbes_facts: Bozano is an art collector and owns paintings by artists including Picasso and contemporary Brazilian painter Beatriz Milhares.

name: Narendrakumar Parekh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025)
forbes_bio: Narendrakumar Parekh is a non-executive director of Pidilite Industries, a company founded by his late brother, Balvant Parekh, in 1959.
He has a minority stake in Pidilite, which is India's leading maker of adhesives and sealants.
His nephew, Madhukar Parekh, chairs the company while his son Apurva Parekh is executive vice chairman.
Pidilite's range of products includes construction chemicals, art materials and organic pigments.
Pidilite is best known for its iconic white glue, Fevicol, popularized over the decades with clever advertising.

name: Roberto Hernandez Ramirez
name_chinese: 罗伯托·赫尔南德斯·拉米雷斯
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Roberto Hernández Ramirez made a fortune in banking, beginning with the establishment of brokerage firm Acciones y Valores, also known as Accival.
Accival purchased Mexican bank Banamex in 1991, becoming Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival, which Hernández chaired.
In 2001 Citigroup purchased Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival for $12 billion in cash and stock.

name: Prathip Chiravanond
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Prathip Chiravanond is part of the clan behind Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Group.
Prathip studied at the University of California, Davis from where he earned degrees in plant sciences, including a doctorate in plant physiology.
He sits on the board of trustees of the International School Bangkok.

name: Alexandre Grendene Bartelle
name_chinese: 亚历山大·格伦德内·巴特勒
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Alexandre Grendene Bartelle and his twin brother Pedro Grendene Bartelle cofounded Grendene, one of the world's largest sandal makers.
In 2013, he stepped down as Grendene's CEO, but has remained as the company's chairman.
He owns 41% of Grendene, which trades on the Sao Paulo exchange.
Alexandre Grendene Bartelle has investments in various industries, from steel to ethanol production and petrochemicals.
He owns real estate in various states in Brazil as well as in Uruguay.

name: Barry Silbert
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Barry Silbert is the founder and CEO of Digital Currency Group (DCG), a conglomerate of five cryptocurrency-focused companies.
DCG's biggest revenue generator: digital asset manager Grayscale, which oversees $23 billion worth of Bitcoin, Ether and other assets.
Through its numerous subsidiaries, DCG has also invested in more than 200 crypto startups.
Prior to launching DCG, Silbert, a former investment banker, sold stock trading platform Second Market to Nasdaq in 2015 for an undisclosed amount.
